How we document a project

Every case study will follow the same format, so you can see the need, the thinking, and the delivery.

  • The need

    The problem or business requirement, described plainly.

  • The solution

    What was proposed, and why it suited the requirement.

  • Services involved

    Which Zeus services were used, linked to their pages.

  • Implementation approach

    How the work was carried out, step by step.

  • Outcomes, where verified

    Results are shown only when they are documented and confirmed.

  • Approved visuals

    Images and screenshots appear only with approval.

How we would approach common requirements

Illustrative scenarios, not completed projects

These are hypothetical examples written to show our approach. They do not describe any client, result, or metric, and they are not part of our project history.

Illustrative scenario

IT Infrastructure, Cloud and Networking

An office whose network has outgrown its setup

Example: small office

The need
A small office has added staff and devices, and the Wi-Fi and wired connections have become slow and inconsistent.
Proposed approach
Assess the premises and existing equipment, then recommend a network layout with suitable switching, structured cabling where needed, and Wi-Fi coverage planned for the space.

Services involved: IT Infrastructure, Cloud and NetworkingIT Managed Services

Implementation approach
  1. Review the premises, the equipment, and how people work.
  2. Propose a network design and scope for approval.
  3. Install and configure the equipment and cabling.
  4. Test coverage and connections before handover.

No outcomes are shown. This is a hypothetical example, not a completed project.

Illustrative scenario

Software Development

Replacing paper-based request tracking

Example: administrative team

The need
Requests arrive by phone, message, and paper form, and it is hard to see what has been approved or completed.
Proposed approach
A custom web-based workflow where requests are submitted, reviewed, approved, and recorded in one place.

Services involved: Software DevelopmentWeb Development

Implementation approach
  1. Document how requests are handled today.
  2. Design the workflow and the information to be recorded.
  3. Build and test with the people who will use it.
  4. Deploy, train users, and refine the system.

No outcomes are shown. This is a hypothetical example, not a completed project.

Illustrative scenario

Web Development

A local business with no online presence

Example: small business

The need
A local business has no website, so potential customers cannot easily find its services or contact details.
Proposed approach
A clear, mobile-friendly business website with the pages and enquiry routes the business needs, set up with hosting and ongoing maintenance.

Services involved: Web Development

Implementation approach
  1. Discuss goals, audience, and content.
  2. Design the page structure and visual style for review.
  3. Build, test across devices, and launch.
  4. Maintain and update the site after launch.

No outcomes are shown. This is a hypothetical example, not a completed project.
